historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 organic guidance (at least 1.5%), Q3-2026 organic growth of 4.7% and a rising DSA backlog, against a pre-2022 organic record in the mid-to-high single digits. Not equity_5yr_cagr - see divergence warning.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (8.4%) diverges by far more than 30% from the 3-year revenue CAGR (0.3%), and the 3-year equity CAGR (2.1%) is depressed by US$434m of goodwill and intangible impairments and US$480m of buybacks in FY2024-25. EPS CAGRs are not meaningful: FY2025 GAAP EPS was -2.91 (impairments) against 7.20 in FY2020 and 9.48 in FY2022. Book value is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: Fiscal years FY2020, FY2022, FY2025. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less cash paid netting shares for withholding tax; no interest-income strip, the company has been in net debt throughout): FY2020 299.7, FY2022 182.6, FY2025 437.3. Owner FCF has grown slightly faster than reported FCF because SBC has been flat at ~70 for five years. The 3-year figures are flattered by a trough base: FY2022 capex was 324.7 (8.2% of revenue) at the peak of the capacity build, against 219.2 in FY2025. FY2025 FCF also includes the since-divested, loss-making CDMO business.

scenario_narratives.base: The biotech-funding recovery that lifted Q3-2026 organic growth to 4.7% and DSA backlog back to US$2.0bn continues but does not return the business to its 2019-22 pace: organic growth of 3.5% in FY2027 peaks at 5% and fades to 3%, with RMS still held back by NIH indirect-cost cuts and DSA carrying the group. Owning Cambodian NHP supply protects the safety-assessment gross margin. Create the Future delivers about a third of its US$300m+ target to the bottom line, taking clean adjusted EBITDA from ~28% to 29.5%, while restructuring and programme costs that management excludes from adjusted earnings keep costing real cash through 2030 and never fully go away. That is a mature unlevered owner-FCF margin of roughly 16%, against ~12% in FY2025 with the loss-making CDMO still inside.
scenario_narratives.bull: A full early-stage R&D upcycle: large pharma rebuilds pre-clinical pipelines, biotech funding normalises, and CRL - with NHP supply secured while smaller CROs remain constrained - takes share in safety assessment at firmer pricing, giving 7%+ organic growth for five years, the pre-2022 norm. Manufacturing, now only Microbial Solutions and Biologics Testing, compounds at high-30s segment margins. Create the Future delivers more than half its target and AI-enabled automation lowers study labour cost, lifting clean adjusted EBITDA to 32%. NAMs turn out to be a service line CRL sells rather than a substitute for in-vivo work.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 pick-up proves to be a restocking bounce. Biotech funding relapses and regulators (FDA 2025 roadmap, UK November 2025 plan) move faster than expected on non-animal New Approach Methodologies, so in-vivo safety assessment and research-model volumes - still the core of DSA and RMS - shrink in real terms; NIH cuts deepen the RMS decline. Revenue is flat to down for two years and grows 2% thereafter. The US$507m Cambodian NHP purchase becomes excess fixed cost on falling study volumes, restructuring becomes permanent rather than transitional, and margins sit ~3 points below base. The securities litigation over NHP imports is an additional, unmodelled cost on this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CRL is valued on what the continuing portfolio can deliver to owners after stock compensation and after the restructuring costs management asks investors to look through. The divestitures genuinely improve the earnings base - the sold businesses were losing money - and that improvement is in the numbers. What is not granted is the adjusted-earnings framing: restructuring has recurred every year since 2023 and is now a declared programme through 2030, so it is charged. The shares have more than doubled from the 52-week low and trade near 29x guided FY2026 non-GAAP EPS; the model shows what cash flows that price requires.
key_risks_to_valuation: The continuing-operations base (revenue 3,850, clean adjusted EBITDA ~28%) is reconstructed from non-GAAP EPS guidance and segment disclosures, not from a published pro-forma; no earnings release with a non-GAAP reconciliation is in the research folder. A 1-point error in the margin base is worth roughly US$9-10 per share in the base case.

The perpetual 0.5% restructuring charge and the 2.0% near-term charge are judgments. If one-off costs really stop after 2030 the base case is too low by a few dollars; if 2026's ~5% of revenue persists it is too high.
Cash tax: a 22.5% rate on EBIT is assumed. Cash tax paid was far lower in 2026 for reasons the 10-Q does not explain beyond the reserve reversal.
NAMs adoption is a slow variable with a wide range; the bear case gives it a 2% terminal growth rate, not decline.
Securities class action and derivative suits over NHP import disclosures are unquantified and not in the bridge.

WACC sensitivity: 55% of base-case enterprise value is terminal value, and each point of WACC moves the base case by roughly US$25-35 per share. Even at a 9% required return the base case is about half the current price.

data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via CRL_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (FY2007-Q3 2026); Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 26 Sep 2026 (balance sheet, cash flow, debt note, EPS reconciliation, acquisitions and divestitures note, restructuring note); Form 10-K FY2025 (treasury-stock netting, lease cost)
data_sources.qualitative: CRL_Analysis.json dated 2026-11-15 (guidance as of the Q3-2026 release on 4 Nov 2026, strategic review, Create the Future, NAMs and NIH risks)

inputs.share_count_basis: 47.876m shares outstanding at 26 Sep 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet) plus 0.781m dilutive options/RSUs/PSUs from the Q3 EPS reconciliation = 48.66m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the buyback programme (US$300m spent in 9M-2026, US$700m authorisation remaining) is what funds the flat count and is not credited separately.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3-2026: cash-flow-statement SBC add-back (FY2025 71.1 - 9M-2025 53.5 + 9M-2026 62.9 = 80.6) plus cash paid netting shares for employee withholding tax (purchase of treasury stock 324.1 less the 300.0 programme repurchases in 9M-2026 = 24.1; Q4-2025 0.1). CRL publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 netting was 10.1 and FY2024 18.5 (FY2025 10-K), so the TTM 24.2 is elevated by the share price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), ERP 5.0%, equity beta ~1.2 (CRL trades as a high-beta biotech-funding proxy) gives cost of equity ~10.3%. Debt is ~12% of enterprise value at a 4.1% weighted coupon plus a floating revolver, ~4.5% after tax. Blended ~9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: the straight-line lease cost (~US$71m/yr) is already an operating expense inside EBITDA, so the operating lease liabilities (US$405m non-current) are NOT in net debt. Finance leases (US$9.7m) are inside total_debt. One treatment, not two.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). Noncontrolling interests are small (net income to NCI US$2.1m in 9M-2026) and are charged once, in the equity bridge: the 10% Noveprim put at the midpoint of its fixed US$47-54m redemption range plus the US$5.1m nonredeemable interest.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, three scenarios, probability-weighted. CRL is a US operating company (non-clinical CRO, research models, QC testing) with no deposit, property-trust or holdco characteristics, so the dcf-methods routing table gives owner-FCF; reference file owner-fcf.md read in full. The Board's strategic review with Elliott concluded in November 2025 with a divest-and-simplify plan, not a sale of the company, so the three-scenario frame stands (no deal-completes/deal-breaks weighting). FRESH BUILD: no prior DCF or Drivers file. | CONTINUING-OPERATIONS NORMALISATION: the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses (sold to GI Partners 6 May 2026, cash PAID to the buyer, US$181.7m pre-tax loss) and certain European Discovery businesses (sold to IQVIA 22 May 2026 for US$126.4m) were ~7% of FY2025 revenue and the Manufacturing segment lost US$71m (FY2024) and US$184m (FY2025) at the operating line because of them. FY2025 and reported TTM FCF therefore are not the base. FY0 is defined as FY2026E on a continuing-operations basis: revenue 3,850 = guided FY2026 reported revenue (~3,945, a 1.5-2.0% decline on 4,015) less ~100 of divested-business revenue still inside Q1 and the first weeks of Q2. Cross-check: H2-2026 (Q3 actual 982.7 + guided Q4 ~960) annualises to ~3,890, i.e. the base plus half a year of growth. Year 1 is FY2027. This also avoids double-counting: the 26 Sep 2026 net debt already contains nine months of FY2026 cash flow, so FY2026 is not projected. | MARGIN BASE: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance of 11.35-11.55 on ~48.9m shares implies non-GAAP operating income of ~820 (~20.5-21% of revenue; CRL's non-GAAP measure is AFTER stock compensation). Adding SBC (~2.1%) and clean depreciation including biological-asset amortisation (~5%) gives adjusted EBITDA before SBC of ~27.5% for FY2026 and ~28% on the continuing portfolio (Manufacturing segment margin rose from ~21% to ~36% once CDMO left). | NON-GAAP LEAKAGE IS CHARGED: CRL has excluded restructuring from adjusted earnings every year since 2023 (US$73m in each of 9M-2025 and 9M-2026, ~two-thirds cash) and in 2026 also ~US$130m of acquisition/integration/divestiture and efficiency-programme fees. Create the Future formally runs through 2030. The ebitda_margin_path is therefore NET of an explicit charge: 2.0% of revenue in FY2027 fading to 0.5% from FY2033 and held there in perpetuity. | CASH TAX: 9M-2026 cash tax paid was only 35.6 against 92.7 a year earlier and 119.6 for FY2025, and the Q3 GAAP tax line carries a one-off US$201m reserve reversal. Neither is carried forward: a 22.5% cash rate on EBIT is used throughout, with no credit for the interest tax shield (~US$25m/yr, a small conservatism). | last_fcf and reported_fcf are TTM to Q3-2026 (OCF 622.4 less capex 222.8) and are LEVERED (after ~US$113m of cash interest), after abnormally low cash tax and after ~US$200m annualised one-off cash costs; they are recorded for audit only, the forward build starts from components. | Interest income is not stripped: the company is in net debt. | Buybacks are real cash (360.7 in FY2025, 324.1 in 9M-2026), so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. | Not in the bridge and unquantified: the NHP-related securities class action and derivative suits; US$48.7m restricted cash.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA before SBC, NET of an explicit restructuring/one-off charge. Clean margin 28.0% in FY2027 rising to 29.5% by FY2031 (about one-third of the US$300m+ Create the Future target reaching the bottom line); charge 2.0% of revenue in FY2027 fading to 0.5% from FY2033, kept in perpetuity.
base.sbc_pct_note: SBC including cash paid on net-share settlement. Latest actual 2.7% (TTM) is inflated by a 24m netting year; 2.1% expense plus ~0.4% netting is the run rate. SBC dollars have been flat at ~70 since FY2021, so only a slow decline is assumed.
base.capex_note: FY2025 capex 5.5% of revenue, 9M-2026 4.5%; 8% in the FY2022-23 capacity build. Held above D&A so the terminal year funds growth. D&A excludes acquired-intangible amortisation (~59/yr and falling), so no tax shield is taken on it.
base.wc_note: Receivables, contract assets and inventory (1,055) exceed payables, deferred revenue and customer deposits, so growth consumes cash: negative capture.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: the bear case is not a solvency case (net debt ~2x EBITDA, no maturity before 2028) but it rests on a structural threat - regulatory substitution of animal testing - layered on a cyclical one, and CRL has just doubled down on NHP supply. Base 50%: guidance, backlog and the cost programme all point this way. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs a funding upcycle, share gains and more than half of an unproven cost programme to arrive together under a new CEO.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
